question: Does PCHP provide a non-redundant pointwise harm contract relative to an equally prefix-causal, non-increasing deployment of the same learned candidate, while retaining material candidate utility?

comparator.name: causal_monotone_candidate
comparator.definition: For each cell in temporal order, q_t=min(q_(t-1),clip(c_t,0,1.3)) with q_0=1.3, where c_t is the frozen raw learned candidate.
comparator.information_boundary: Uses exactly the same frozen learned candidate at each record, no future record, no target outcome, and O(1) online state; it enforces the same physical range and non-increase but omits the protected-state harm tube.
comparator.purpose: Closest operational control for whether the pointwise harm contract is empirically active and whether PCHP retains useful candidate information. It is not claimed to implement the full adversarial online-isotonic-regression algorithm of Kotlowski et al.

metrics.accuracy: For each method, average absolute error across records within cell, average cells equally within domain, then average the 12 domains equally.
metrics.pointwise_harm: For absolute loss, the exact outcome-uniform harm relative to the selected protected state is absolute prediction displacement. A violation is abs(q_t-b_t)>0.01+1e-12.
metrics.utility_retention: If the causal monotone candidate improves the baseline, retention=(MAE_baseline-MAE_PCHP)/(MAE_baseline-MAE_candidate). If it does not improve, retention is not used and PCHP must itself improve the baseline.
metrics.uncertainty: 100000 percentile bootstrap resamples of the 12 paired complete-domain effects with seed 20260805; descriptive because all development domains were previously opened.

frozen_gates.contract_activity: The causal monotone candidate violates the delta=0.01 pointwise contract in at least 9 of 12 domains and in at least 25% of the 586 physical cells, while PCHP has zero violations within tolerance.
frozen_gates.utility: Either the causal monotone candidate does not improve the protected baseline and PCHP does, or PCHP retains at least 50% of the candidate's positive domain-equal MAE gain.
frozen_gates.information_and_order: All row keys and truths agree across frozen inputs; q is prefix-causal by construction, lies in [0,1.3], is non-increasing within every cell, and uses no outcome in construction.
frozen_gates.reproducibility: Input hashes match, all 12 domains and 586 cells are present, and an independent loop replay from frozen raw candidates reproduces every computed q_t value exactly.

decision_rule.RETAIN: All four gates pass. Permit a closest-operational-control result and a bounded safety-utility-frontier interpretation.
decision_rule.NARROW: Information/order and reproducibility pass, but exactly one of contract_activity or utility fails. Retain only as an appendix boundary without a central frontier claim.
decision_rule.REJECT: Information/order or reproducibility fails, or both contract_activity and utility fail. Do not add the comparator to the manuscript.
decision_rule.stop_rule: No threshold, aggregation, domain roster, candidate definition, or budget change after inspecting results.

chronology_boundary: The underlying development outcomes have been opened previously. This pre-freeze prevents further analysis drift but cannot convert the result into prospective or confirmatory evidence.
